description: Huh7 sorafenib-resistant HCC cell line (Huh7SR)
cell line: Huh7SR
parental cell line: Huh7
drug exposure: Fostamatinib
treatment dose: 2 uM
treatment length: 24 hr
Drug solutions were prepared in cell culture media to reach a final concentraiton of 2uM.
Huh7SR cells were treated with either DMSO (2uM) or fostamatinib (2uM) 24 hr. Drug treatments were applied in triplicate per condition.
Illumina HCS 3.4.0 software was used for basecalling.
Fastq files containing sequenced reads were mapped to the human genome h19 using Hiearchical Indexing for Spliced Alignment of Transcripts (HISAT).
Raw read counts for each gene were quanitfied using featureCounts software and the GENCODE v.22 Gene Transfer Format (GTF) file as a transcript reference (GENCODE annotation).
Genes with read counts below 5 for at least 2 samples out of 3 within each group were filtered out.
Read counts were normalized using the TMM method.

For RNA-seq data, sequenced reads were trimmed for adaptor sequence by cutadapt, and then mapped to hg38 whole genome using hisat2 v1.1.0 with default parameters

For RNA-seq data, unique mapped reads were extracted; featureCounts v1.6.1 with parameters -T 16 -p -t exon -g gene_id was used to obtain read counts of all genes; the version of GTF files is gencode.v35
For RNA-seq data, DESeq2 was used to perform normalized to read count matrices and obtain differential genes with pvalue 0.01 and Foldchange 2 as the threashold
For ATAC seq data, sequenced reads were trimmed for adaptor sequence by cutadapt, and then mapped to hg38 whole genome using bowtie2 v2.4.1 with parameters, -X 1000

For ATAC seq data, PCR duplicates were removed with Picard. Mitochondria data and low quality reads were removed with samtools. Peaks were called by MACS2 with parameters --shift -75 --extsize 150 --nomodel -B --SPMR -g hs --keep-dup all.

To establish sorafenib-resistant (SR) HCC cells, the cells were treated with increasing concentrations of sorafenib from 1 to 10 µM over a period of 6 months. Con and SR Cells were treated with DMSO (Con), Regorafenib (5 uM).

The HCC cell line Huh7 (https://cellbank.snu.ac.kr/eng/tmpl/sub_main.php?m_cd=46&m_id=0201&sp=2&c_id=769) was purchased from the Korean Cell Line Bank (Seoul, Korea) and cultured in MEM supplemented with 10 % heat-inactivated FBS, penicillin, and streptomycin (Thermo Fisher Scientific, Waltham, MA, USA) at 37 °C in a humidified atmosphere with 95 % air / 5 % CO2.
Illumina CASAVA v1.8.2 software was used for basecalling.
To avoid low-quality data, we clipped and trimmed the reads using Trimmomatic (v0.33)

For the analysis of differentially expressed genes, the data of quality-checked reads for each condition were processed with the STAR (version 2.7.1) software based on reference genome sequence (The GENCODE Homo sapiens reference sequence GRCh38 (Release 27) and the differential gene expressed values of each sample were calculated by the DESeq2 Bioconductor package.
The number of reads mapped to gene ID features were counted using STAR.
Assembly: The GENCODE Homo sapiens reference sequence GRCh38 (Release 27)

Following attachment, cells were treated with different drug compound. The control group was treated with complete medium only. After treatment for 48 h, cells were collected and snHH-seq was performed for single-cell screening
Cells were seeded in a 6-well plate at a density of 1×105 cells/well and cultured overnight.

For sequencing library, the poly-A tail was trimmed from each raw sequencing read using Cutadapt. Subsequently, real cells were identified based on the number of reads per cell, utilizing a manually defined minimal read cutoff determined by the results of the UMI-tools whitelist function. Reads were then aligned to the GRCh38 reference genome using the STAR 2-pass mode, and only uniquely mapped reads were retained. Each read was assigned to its corresponding gene using the “gene” tag within the GRCh38 GTF by employing feature Count. The digital gene expression (DGE) was generated using the UMI tools count function. Batches were defined as each sequencing library for each patient. For each batch, quality control (QC) was performed using Scanpy. Low-quality cells or potential doublets were removed by applying a manually defined cutoff for the number of UFIs and genes per cell, and genes expressed in less than 0.25% of the cells were also removed.
